title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A busy but mostly manageable day: President Trump kicked off a big Asia trip, United had a short tech hiccup after a rough week for air travel, and flu season is picking up just in time for Thanksgiving. Closer to home for Charlotte readers there's news on a mold cleanup and a $300 million community fund, plus Jamaica gets approval for Ozempic. And yes, there's a rescued puppy who now works at a car dealership.

stories.headline: Trump heads to Asia for summits, including a first-ever meeting with Xi and Putin
stories.summary: President Trump landed in Manila for the ASEAN summit, where he's meeting with leaders of Japan, Australia and India and signing a trade deal with Thailand. He then goes to Shenzhen, China, for the APEC summit and a first-of-its-kind three-way meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin focused on nuclear disarmament. Some U.S. allies are reportedly nervous the talks could stray into Ukraine or Taiwan. It's his first trip abroad since his party's big midterm losses.
key_facts: First stop: ASEAN summit in Manila, Philippines; then APEC in Shenzhen, China
The Xi-Putin-Trump meeting is expected Wednesday, with nuclear disarmament on the agenda
Trump said a meeting with North Korea's Kim Jong Un is possible, but 'up to President Xi'
The U.S. and China extended a trade truce last week that runs to early January
disputed: A possible Kim Jong Un meeting is unconfirmed; Trump said 'He may come, I don't know.'
Trump said he won't raise spying allegations tied to Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, who left after admitting an affair with an alleged Chinese government agent; Beijing says it wasn't involved.
stories.why: A three-way nuclear conversation between these leaders has never happened before, so what comes out of it could shape global security and trade.

stories.headline: United's brief outage is fixed, and air travel is mostly back on track
stories.summary: United Airlines had a systemwide tech outage Monday that held up departing flights for roughly 90 minutes before it was resolved. The airline said there was no sign of a cyberattack, and flights already in the air weren't affected. It came right after Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop, which caused thousands of delays and cancellations. Charlotte's airport saw only one United flight affected.
key_facts: United reported 28 cancellations and 811 delays by Monday night, about 25% of its flights that day
Friday's ground stop led to 571 cancellations at Charlotte on Friday alone
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the United issue wasn't an FAA system problem
Separately, a 'software bug' at JPMorgan Chase caused online banking and Zelle hiccups Monday
stories.why: With Thanksgiving travel around the corner, it's reassuring that things are largely back to normal, though it's worth checking your flight status before heading out.

stories.headline: Flu season started early, and there's still time for a shot before Thanksgiving
stories.summary: CDC tracking shows flu activity has climbed above the national baseline, which signals that flu season has started in earnest, and earlier than usual. Experts say a flu shot takes about 10 days to reach full strength, so getting one now still covers Thanksgiving gatherings. The season has already been serious for some families, with two child deaths reported. RSV and COVID levels are low for now, but doctors still recommend staying up to date on boosters.
key_facts: Outpatient visits for flu-like illness are at 3.2%, above the 2.9% national baseline
A flu shot takes about 10 days to fully kick in
AAA expects about 82 million people to travel over Thanksgiving
Flu, COVID and RSV vaccines are widely available at pharmacies
disputed: Flu shots are an established, approved vaccine. They don't guarantee you won't catch the flu, but they make hospitalization less likely.
stories.why: This is an easy, practical step you can take this week to stay healthier over the holidays.

stories.headline: Mooresville elementary school stays remote another week for mold cleanup
stories.summary: Coddle Creek Elementary in Iredell County will stay closed to in-person learning for a second week while crews keep cleaning possible mold. The district says a lab told them more cleaning is needed, and the school board approved a new cleanup contract Monday. Some parents say the district knew about the issue since summer and want accountability and an apology.
key_facts: Students haven't had in-person classes since Nov. 6
Cleanup includes air duct cleaning, misting classrooms and running commercial scrubbers
The district earlier said there was no immediate threat to health and safety
The official lab testing report hadn't been received as of Monday
stories.why: If your family is connected to the school, this means remote learning continues this week while the cleanup wraps up.

stories.headline: Charlotte sets up a group to help decide how $300M in I-77 community money gets spent
stories.summary: Charlotte City Council voted 9-1 to approve guidelines for a working group that will help shape how $300 million from the state is spent in neighborhoods along the planned I-77 South toll lane project. Ideas floated so far include a recreation center, transportation upgrades and grocery stores. Some west Charlotte residents have opposed the highway expansion over pollution and community division concerns, and council members say affected residents should lead this process.
key_facts: NCDOT pledged $300 million for community investments
The vote was 9-1 at a special meeting Nov. 16
Applications to join the group are open for one week
The goal is to have members in place by the end of the year
stories.why: If you live near the corridor, this is a real chance to have a say in how a big pot of money is used in your neighborhood.

stories.headline: Jamaica explores AI infrastructure, and people have questions
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andrew Holness said the government approved a memorandum of understanding to explore building artificial intelligence infrastructure in Jamaica. The announcement is drawing scrutiny, with concerns about water and power use and environmental impact.
key_facts: The government approved an MOU to explore AI infrastructure
Concerns center on water and electricity demand and the environment
stories.why: AI facilities can use a lot of resources, so this is an early-stage conversation worth following for anyone in Jamaica.

stories.headline: Former DPP Paula Llewellyn tells graduates: serve with humility
stories.summary: Speaking to Jamaica Theological Seminary's Class of 2026, former Director of Public Prosecutions Paula Llewellyn urged graduates not to let status go to their heads. She shared that she offers a cool drink of water to sanitation workers at her complex, who told her the gesture is rare. She encouraged treating public work as a vocation, even when it feels thankless.
key_facts: Llewellyn spent 41 years in public service
She spoke at the seminary's graduation on Saturday
stories.why: It's a nice reminder that small acts of kindness stick with people.

links.title: Llewellyn: Don’t let status go to your head

stories.headline: Jamaica's inflation eases slightly, but bills are still biting
stories.summary: Jamaica's annual inflation dipped to 8.2% in October from 8.6% in September, according to STATIN. Monthly prices rose 0.3%, driven mostly by higher electricity, water and sewage charges. Transport and food costs remain well above last year's levels.
key_facts: Annual inflation: 8.2% in October, versus 2.9% a year earlier
Transport costs are up 15.0% year over year
Food prices are up 10.9%
Electricity, gas and other fuels rose 3.5% in October alone
stories.why: The pace is easing a little, but household budgets are still feeling pressure from utilities, food and getting around.
